questions.q: What is Copilot in Fabric, structurally?
options: An AI experience embedded directly into the Fabric item you're working in — a notebook, KQL queryset, report, or pipeline — not a separate chat product
A standalone chat application unrelated to Fabric items
A feature only available in Power BI, not in notebooks
A one-time code generator that only runs during workspace setup
questions.explain: Each Fabric surface gets a Copilot experience tailored to what you're doing there — this lesson focuses specifically on the notebook experience.

questions.q: What is the practical difference between the chat pane and in-cell Copilot in a Fabric notebook?
options: The chat pane handles multi-step workflows across several cells with a reviewable diff; in-cell Copilot is scoped to slash commands on a single cell
They are identical in every respect
In-cell Copilot works across the whole notebook while the chat pane only works on one cell
The chat pane cannot generate any code at all
questions.explain: Chat pane: multi-step, multi-cell, reviewable diff. In-cell: /explain, /fix, /comments, /optimize, scoped to one cell.

questions.q: What does it mean that Copilot in a Fabric notebook is 'schema-aware'?
options: It understands the attached lakehouse's actual tables, files, and recent execution telemetry, so answers are grounded in your real workspace
It can only answer questions about schemas defined in SQL Server
It ignores the lakehouse entirely and answers from general training data only
Schema-awareness means it never needs review before applying changes
questions.explain: You can ask plain questions like 'how many tables are in the lakehouse?' and get an answer grounded in the real attached lakehouse, not a generic guess.

questions.q: What happens when a cell or Spark job fails and Fix with Copilot appears?
options: It shows an error summary, a root-cause guess, and a suggested fix you can review as a diff before it's applied
It automatically rewrites the entire notebook without any review
It deletes the failed cell permanently
It disables the notebook until a human rewrites the code from scratch
questions.explain: Fix with Copilot uses the same approval-diff pattern as the chat pane — you review the suggested fix before committing to it.

questions.q: What is the default behavior before Copilot runs a cell or applies an edit, and why does it matter?
options: Copilot asks for your approval by default — a guardrail that keeps a human in the loop before anything executes
Copilot always runs changes immediately with no approval step
Approval is only required for KQL queries, never for PySpark code
The approval step can never be disabled under any settings
questions.explain: That default is the mechanism that keeps a human reviewing Copilot's work — the same guardrail theme Lesson 56 returns to later in this chapter.
